correctness.rationale: The open neighborhood face test is that the intersection of the vertex neighborhoods is nonempty, using symmetry of adjacency. An independently written bit-mask calculation tested all 2^13 subsets, giving the augmented face vector (1,13,78,221,195,78,13). It checked cone fillings of all 65 absent triangular loops. The one-skeleton is complete so triangular loops generate its fundamental group, and the fillings kill them. The same program reproduced 218 free-face collapses with the published ordering and face vector (13,68,81) in the remaining two-dimensional complex; an alternative legal order gives another two-dimensional complex. Thus simple connectivity, reduced Euler characteristic 25, Hurewicz and the homology version of Whitehead yield a wedge of 25 two-spheres. Independently, augmented boundary ranks over F₁₀₁ were (1,12,66,130,65,13). They are lower bounds on rational ranks, imply zero rational reduced Betti numbers outside degree 2, and rational Euler characteristic forces degree 2 to have dimension 25. All 78 affine maps were then checked by enumerating unions of vertex cycles. A fixed face that is a union of k cycles contributes (−1)^(k−1) including orientation and the augmented empty term. Summing yields −1 for twelve nontrivial translations, 1 for each of the 65 elements with multiplier different from 1, and 25 for the identity, with the displayed signed contributions by dimension reproduced for each multiplier. The Hopf trace formula now gives exactly the stated H₂ character. The proposed rational permutation-plus-augmentation module has that character, and semisimplicity and characteristic-zero character comparison identify the rational modules. No supplied code was executed.
residual_risks: This character check does not identify integral group-module structure or the action of any larger automorphism group. The modular boundary computation alone is not an integral homotopy certificate; the independent collapses and triangular fillings supply that step.

originality.rationale: The exact claimed rational action is mechanically forced by a distinct same-day theorem that either of two 39-element affine orbits of oriented tetrahedral sphere classes generates H₂, of rank 25. The representative {0,1,3,11} has stabilizer H generated by x↦1−x, an even permutation on its carrier, so its oriented class is fixed by H and yields an equivariant surjection ℚ[A/H]→H₂. The translation subgroup N=C₁₃ acts freely on the 39 cosets with three orbits, so the target has at most three N-invariants. Its dimension is 25 and the only nontrivial rational irreducible of N has dimension 12, so there is exactly one invariant dimension and two copies of that irreducible on restriction. The invariant line is fixed by all of A: the invariants in the source are ℚ[C₆/C₂], on which the action factors through C₃, which has no nontrivial rational one-dimensional representation. Every nonidentity multiplier permutes the nontrivial complex N-weights without a fixed weight, so has trace zero on their sum. This gives 25, −1 and 1, hence the exact module. Same-day ordering is unknown; this is a coverage decision, not a claim of earlier discovery. A distinct later record also explicitly states the identical module and character.
residual_risks: Chronological priority within 2026-10-18 is not established. Unavailable cited texts and irrelevant search results are not negative evidence. Neither limitation changes the explicit same-day implication.
